metaData.title: Can AI Write Your Code?
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: A case study evaluates ChatGPT-4.0 Pro's ability to generate code for causal inference tasks in Python, R, and Stata, finding better performance in Python and R, while emphasizing the continued need for human expertise and validation.
metaData.summary: This article reviews a study by Winberg et al. that systematically evaluates ChatGPT-4.0 Pro's coding capabilities for quantitative research, specifically for causal inference methods like Difference-in-Differences, Inverse Probability Treatment Weighting, and Regression Discontinuity. The study uses benchmark solutions from 'Causal Inference: The Mixtape' and assesses performance across Python, R, and Stata based on accuracy, efficiency, errors, editing needs, and consistency. Results show ChatGPT performs better in Python and R than in Stata. The author then shares personal reflections on how LLMs have transformed their own workflow, including a strategic shift from SAS and RStudio to Python and VS Code, and the acceleration of data collection and analysis tasks. The article concludes that while AI is a powerful accelerator, human supervision, validation, and expertise remain essential, and that the tool's rise will create new dynamics in knowledge production and inequality.

mainPoints.point: ChatGPT-4.0 Pro performs better in Python and R than in Stata for causal inference coding tasks.
mainPoints.explanation: The study found that ChatGPT generated accurate code and results in Python and R for most tasks, while Stata was less reliable, likely due to the abundance of public code examples for Python and R.

mainPoints.point: Human supervision and validation remain essential when using AI-generated code.
mainPoints.explanation: The risk of hallucination and errors persists, as highlighted by the EY Canada study incident. Researchers must check assumptions, validate data, test code, and compare results with benchmarks.

mainPoints.point: LLMs are accelerating workflow changes, influencing language and tool choices.
mainPoints.explanation: The author's team shifted from SAS and RStudio to Python and VS Code due to better AI support, demonstrating that AI is not just a productivity tool but also shapes infrastructure and strategic decisions.

mainPoints.point: AI lowers the barrier to knowledge production but creates new challenges.
mainPoints.explanation: While AI enables faster content creation and idea sharing, it also leads to a more crowded internet and potential inequality between those who use AI effectively and those who do not.

keyQuotes: What if the real question is no longer whether AI can write code, but whether we can trust the code it writes?
We can use LLMs to work faster, but not to remove the responsibility of the researcher.
AI may make writing faster, but it will not replace curiosity, discipline, and the desire to contribute something meaningful.
The more powerful the tool becomes, the more necessary it is to know when to trust it and when not to.
In my work, I see them more as very fast research assistants than as autonomous experts.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Introduces GPT-5.5: A New Class of Intelligence for Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces GPT-5.5, a new model designed for complex goal understanding and autonomous task completion, now available in ChatGPT and Codex.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing workspace agents in ChatGPT
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI 正式推出 ChatGPT Workspace Agents，这是一种无需编程、通过自然语言即可创建的 AI 智能体，能够深度集成 Slack、Linear、GitHub 等工作工具，实现 24/7 全天候的任务自动化与工作流辅助。

relatedArticles.title: Your ReAct Agent Is Wasting 90% of Its Retries — Here’s How to Stop It
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article identifies a critical architectural flaw in ReAct-style LLM agents where hallucinated tool names waste the majority of retry budgets, and proposes three structural fixes—error taxonomy, per-tool circuit breakers, and deterministic tool routing—to eliminate this waste and improve production reliability.

relatedArticles.title: GPT-5.5 Instant: smarter, clearer, and more personalized
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI releases GPT-5.5 Instant as the new default ChatGPT model, delivering significant improvements in factuality, conciseness, and personalization through better context usage and new memory controls.

relatedArticles.title: Workspace agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article from the OpenAI Blog introduces the concept of workspace agents in ChatGPT, explaining their core components, design anatomy, common workflow patterns, and providing a practical guide for using, building, testing, and scaling these agents for repeatable, structured business tasks.

relatedArticles.title: The Multi-Agent Trap
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article analyzes the 'Multi-Agent Trap' where unstructured AI architectures amplify errors, providing a research-backed playbook of proven patterns and failure prevention strategies for production-grade agentic systems.

relatedArticles.title: Hybrid Search and Re-Ranking in Production RAG
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article presents a production-grade approach to improving RAG retrieval quality by combining hybrid search (BM25 + dense vectors) with cross-encoder re-ranking and metadata filtering, supported by real-world evaluation metrics.

relatedArticles.title: Building an Evaluation Harness for Production AI Agents: A 12-Metric Framework From 100+ Deployments
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article presents a comprehensive 12-metric evaluation framework for production AI agents, distilled from over 100 enterprise deployments, covering retrieval, generation, agent behavior, and production health.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.4 Thinking and GPT-5.4 Pro
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces the rollout of GPT-5.4 Thinking and Pro models, integrating advanced reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows into a single frontier model.

relatedArticles.title: Stop Treating AI Memory Like a Search Problem
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article critiques the conventional 'store-and-retrieve' approach to AI memory, proposing a lifecycle-based system with decay, contradiction detection, confidence scoring, compression, and expiry to manage memory like a human brain rather than a static archive.
